episodes.title: Michkov Wants Out + Inside Sports Business with Ziyan Hemani
paragraphs: The boys are back in the box, and this week we’ve got a special guest. Ziyan Hemani of Tennis Canada joins us to talk about working in the business of sports.

Around the league, Shane Wright is off to an explosive start in Nashville, the Ducks are in extension talks with Joel Quenneville, and Matvei Michkov has requested a trade. On the international stage, Canada went 4-0 in the prelims at the women’s championship in Denmark and beat Czechia 3-2 in the quarterfinals. Next up is Finland on Sunday at 7 AM PCT / 9 AM ET.

We also step off the ice to break down Rashee Rice’s bankruptcy filing. Despite a $6.5 million contract with the Chiefs, he’s facing roughly $3 million in claims from his 2024 car crash and has put up his Super Bowl ring to cover legal fees.

In Oilers news, Tristan Jarry stood tall against Philly, McDavid strings together back-to-back point games, and Devon Levi returns looking sharp. That sets up an interesting goalie situation once Andersen is back.
Player of the Week is Jake Guentzel, with 9 points and a +6 in four games. Nikita Kucherov grabs the honourable mention with 8 points.

episodes.title: McDavid Breaks Gretzky’s Record + Redrafting the 2010 Class
paragraphs: The boys are back in the box, and Connor McDavid just did something even Gretzky couldn’t. He’s the fastest player ever to 30 assists in a season, getting there in 15 games and topping Wayne’s record of 16.

Around the league, we break down the biggest choke of the season so far in Winnipeg vs. Montreal. Seattle sends Shane Wright to Nashville for Matthew Wood, and Kucherov reportedly turns down $20M a year because he wants to play with a top forward. We also get into Canada’s decision on Russian and Belarusian players, and the Misa-for-Edvinsson offer Detroit turned down. Plus, Canada rolls Sweden 5-0 at the women’s tournament in Denmark.

In Oilers news, we dig into the growing Ducks rivalry, preview Canucks vs. Oilers, share our hot takes on the Hometown jerseys, and celebrate Nuge becoming the franchise’s all-time leader in games played with 1,038.

Then we rewind to the 2010 draft and rank its top 10: Stone, Tarasenko, Hall, Seguin, Andersen and more, with a shoutout to Zach Hyman. Eshan’s Player of the Week is Cutter Gauthier, who scored 7 goals in 3 games. Jack Hughes grabs the honourable mention.

episodes.title: Brewers Are Champs (Ilyas Called It) + Re-Drafting the 2009 Class
paragraphs: The boys are back in the box, and the Brewers are World Series champions! Milwaukee closes it out 4-1, and yes, Ilyas called it. We break down a dominant postseason from the pitching staff, led by Ilyas’s MVP Aaron Ashby, who threw 18 scoreless innings with 20 strikeouts and three saves.

Back on the ice, Dylan Larkin gets suspended, Nikita Kucherov is on the move in a blockbuster trade, and we recap Ducks vs. Canucks. In Oilers news, Devon Levi is back skating, Hyman picks up another injury but is skating too, and Jason Dickinson finally returns to the lineup.
Then we rewind to the 2009 draft and rank its top 10: Hedman, O’Reilly, Tavares, Duchene, Kadri, Kreider and more.
Ilyas’s Player of the Week is Jacob Fowler: 3 wins, a .980 save percentage, and a 43-save shutout. Drake Batherson grabs the honourable mention with 8 points in 3 games.

episodes.title: The Hellebuyck Blockbuster & McDavid Goes Nuclear
paragraphs: The boys are back in the box, and the trade market just exploded. Connor Hellebuyck is headed to New Jersey, and Winnipeg gets back Nico Daws, Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Alexander Command and a pair of picks. Who won it? We also cover Brady Tkachuk’s return to Ottawa, Quinn Hughes heading back to Vancouver, and the leaked Hometown Remix jerseys, including the Oilers’ “Oil Country After Midnight.”
We kick things off at the World Series, where the Brewers take Game 1 over the Rays, 3-2. William Contreras drove in a run and made two huge throws, while Liam Hicks drove in both Rays runs.

In Oilers news, Devon Levi heads to IR for three weeks, Jason Dickinson’s return is imminent and Ekholm will miss three games. Then we rewind to the 2008 draft and rank its top 10: Stamkos, Doughty, Karlsson, Josi, Pietrangelo and more.
Eshan’s Player of the Week is an easy one: Connor McDavid, with 13 points in just three games. Leon Draisaitl takes the honourable mention with 9 points of his own.

episodes.title: Kaprizov Is Cooking + Who Really Won the 2007 Draft?
paragraphs: The boys are back in the box with a loaded week around the league. Hellebuyck is cleared to return for the Jets on Friday, Aatu Raty gets moved for Jacob Quillan and Brandon Buhr, and Matt Duchene goes under the knife for core surgery. We also break down Bedard’s debut, Roger McQueen’s first NHL game, DeBrincat’s big 7-year extension and Stenberg’s first career goal.

We take a quick detour to the diamond: the Dodgers get swept, and the Rays and Guardians battle it out. Then it’s back to Edmonton for some Oilers hockey cards, plus injury updates. Hyman, Dach and Walman are set to return, Dickson and Nuge aren’t far behind, and McDavid hits career game 800.

Kirill Kaprizov takes Player of the Week with 6 goals, 4 assists, a +7 and a hat trick in four games. Brady Tkachuk grabs the honourable mention with two hat tricks of his own. To close it out, we rewind to the 2007 draft and rank its top 10: Kane, Benn, Subban, Pacioretty and more.

episodes.title: Goalie Graveyard ft. Troy Wansink
paragraphs: The boys are back in the box, and this week the goalie world is on fire. Shesterkin is done for the season and Korpisalo is out four weeks. Does Helly make sense as the fix? We also take a detour to the Hellebucks website, because of course we do.

Over in Oil Country, Levi looked sharp against the Ducks, Jarry finally gets his first win, Hyman is close to coming back, and Dach goes down injured. Plus, Drai and Podz have chemistry that just doesn’t make sense, in the best way.

Then we sit down with Troy Wansink for an interview you won’t want to miss. We also share our honest thoughts on Mitch Marner and crown our Player of the Week: Kyle Connor, who went absolutely off with 5 goals, 1 assist and a +5. Jake Oettinger grabs the honourable mention.

episodes.title: Podkolzin Is Scoring 50. Book It.
paragraphs: The NHL season is officially underway, and there’s already plenty to talk about.

The boys break down the biggest stories from the season openers, including Carolina’s early Stanley Cup hangover, Washington looking dangerous with its new additions, Matthew Knies shining for Columbus, St. Louis shutting out Dallas, and Igor Shesterkin scoring a goalie goal. They also discuss Aleksander Barkov landing on LTIR and new captaincies for David Pastrnak in Boston and Thomas Chabot in Ottawa.

Then it’s time to talk Oilers, and things are already falling apart. Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Zach Hyman are dealing with injuries, Edmonton is in shambles, and Ilyas is ready to make the boldest prediction of the season: Podkolzin is scoring 50.
Draft Class Rewind returns with the 2006 class as the boys rank Jonathan Toews, Jordan Staal, Brad Marchand, Claude Giroux, Phil Kessel and more.
Finally, Evan Bouchard takes Player of the Week after putting up 4 goals and 4 assists with a +5 rating, while Connor McDavid earns the honourable mention with 7 points of his own.

episodes.title: Captain Celebrini
paragraphs: The boys are back with the latest news from around the hockey world, starting with a new wave of contracts. They break down Adam Fantilli’s massive six-year deal, along with new contracts for Sam Steel and Oliver Moore.

There are also new leaders around the league, with Mikael Granlund taking over as captain in Anaheim and Macklin Celebrini getting the C in San Jose. The boys also dive into the latest Kirill Marchenko rumors, with Boston, Edmonton, Toronto, and Montreal all in the conversation.

Then it’s an Oilers update as Jason Dickinson is expected to miss the start of the season and Edmonton is linked to Kirby Dach. They also discuss the PWHL expanding its presence on Hockey Night in Canada.

Finally, Draft Class Rewind is back. The boys revisit the legendary 2005 NHL Draft and re-rank a class featuring Sidney Crosby, Carey Price, Anze Kopitar, Kris Letang, Jonathan Quick, Tuukka Rask, and more.
Twenty years later, who really should have gone where?

episodes.title: These NHL Predictions Could Age Horribly
paragraphs: The NHL season is almost here, which means it’s time to put our predictions on the record.

The boys start with the latest news around the league, including new captaincies for Connor Bedard and Drew Doughty, Ryan Reaves announcing his retirement, and another huge wave of contracts featuring Ryan Leonard, Drake Batherson, Cutter Gauthier, Jordan Staal, and more. They also break down the Oilers’ leadership group, with Connor McDavid wearing the C alongside Leon Draisaitl, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins, Evan Bouchard, and Zach Hyman.
Then it’s prediction time. Ilyas and Eshan make their picks for the Hart, Art Ross, Rocket Richard, Ted Lindsay, Conn Smythe, Vezina, Norris, Selke, Calder, Jack Adams, and Presidents’ Trophy.

Finally, they predict all four NHL divisions from top to bottom. From Edmonton and Florida at the top to some bold predictions for San Jose, Montreal, Minnesota, and more, the takes are officially locked in.
Plus, an update on the Kawhi Leonard trade. The receipts start now on Brothers in the Box.

episodes.title: Dylan Hewlett Joins the Show
paragraphs: The boys are joined by Dylan Hewlett for a special interview before breaking down another busy week across the sports world.

In the NHL, Dylan Larkin reports to Red Wings training camp without the captaincy, while Connor Ingram and John Klingberg announce their retirements. The boys discuss Ingram’s decision to step away from hockey and study psychology before reacting to the latest signings, including Chris Kreider, Zachary Bolduc, Alex Formenton, Brayden Bowman, and Mark Stone.
Then it’s over to the NFL, where the Lions barely escape against the Saints, the Rams fall in Australia, and Myles Garrett is expected to miss time following knee surgery.
They also check in on the US Open before sitting down with Dylan Hewlett to talk sports, his journey, and plenty more on another episode of Brothers in the Box.

episodes.title: The NBA Just HAMMERED the Clippers
paragraphs: The boys break down major news surrounding the Los Angeles Clippers, including a reported $3 million fine, the loss of five first-round picks, Steve Ballmer’s suspension, and additional penalties involving Kawhi Leonard and members of the organization.
Then it’s over to the NHL with Eeli Tolvanen joining the Rangers, the Robert Thomas captaincy discussion, and Zeev Buium’s massive eight-year extension.

The episode also covers the difficult situation involving Matthew Mayich, including his reported condition, allegations surrounding the workout at Arizona State, and questions raised by his family’s lawyer about how the situation was handled.

episodes.title: Makar Broke the Bank
paragraphs: The boys are back with another packed episode, starting with some massive NHL storylines. They react to Cale Makar’s reported 8-year, $20.4 million deal and dive into Connor Hellebuyck publicly requesting a trade. Where could Hellebuyck end up, what would a deal cost, and does he actually get moved?
They also discuss potential changes to the NHL broadcast world, with Kevin Bieksa and Elliotte Friedman potentially heading to Amazon and Kelly Hrudey reportedly not returning.
Outside of hockey, the boys check in on Week 0 of college football, talk Tour Championship golf, and then finish things off with 20 Questions.

episodes.title: No Sitting on the Fence
paragraphs: The boys are putting their predictions to the test with a full What’s More Likely? episode.

From McDavid chasing 140 points and Matthews pushing for 70 goals to Bedard vs. Celebrini, Makar vs. Hughes, playoff droughts, Stanley Cup contenders, fantasy hockey, and potential blockbuster trades, Ilyas and Eshan have to pick which outcome they think has the better chance of happening.
Some choices are easy. Others might expose some seriously questionable hockey takes.

episodes.title: Blue Jays Blow it Up
paragraphs: The boys are back to break down another week of headlines from around the sports world, starting with the latest Zach Werenski trade rumors, as reports suggest a deal with the Dallas Stars is still on the table. They discuss what a blockbuster trade could look like and whether Columbus should finally pull the trigger.

They also celebrate Canada's dominant 8-1 victory at the Gretzky Hlinka Cup, react to the Kings announcing they'll retire Anže Kopitar's number and unveil a bronze statue, and dive into the latest off-ice stories, including Jack Hughes and Tate McRae and the controversy surrounding Kawhi Leonard's reported $100 million Daktronics sponsorship.

To wrap things up, the boys break down the Blue Jays' deadline shakeup, discussing the departures of Kevin Gausman, Daulton Varsho, Jeff Hoffman, and top prospect Arjun Nimmala, while evaluating the return package led by José Soriano, Spencer Arrighetti, and Josh Smith. Did Toronto make the right move, or are they setting themselves back?

episodes.title: Rating the NHL’s Most Unhinged Fanbases
paragraphs: The boys break down the latest NHL signings, including massive deals for Macklin Celebrini, Patrick Kane, Jason Robertson, Cole Sillinger, Jet Greaves, and John Marino. They debate which contracts are worth the money and which teams may regret their decisions.

Then it’s an Oilers update, with Matt Savoie’s agent making it clear that the young forward wants to stay in Edmonton. The guys discuss what a future extension could look like, why the Oilers are focused on winning now, and whether Tristan Jarry should enter the season as the clear starting goaltender.

They also react to LeBron potentially heading to Philadelphia before introducing a special new segment: rating NHL fanbases. Which supporters are loyal, which are chaotic, and which ones are completely unbearable?

episodes.title: The Worlds Game
paragraphs: The boys are back to make their official World Cup predictions, breaking down who they think will win it all before previewing one of the biggest matches of the tournament: England vs. France. They recap the latest action and debate which nation has the best path to lifting the trophy.

Then it's over to the NHL, where free agency continues to heat up. They react to Connor Bedard's monster extension, discuss why Chicago should do everything they can to bring Patrick Kane back, and break down new deals for Jamie Drysdale, Trevor Zegras, Kirby Dach, Cole Perfetti, Anthony Mantha, and Braden Schneider. The boys also discuss the end of an era in Detroit as Steve Yzerman steps down.

episodes.title: McGregor is Back
paragraphs: The boys break down an action-packed week in sports, starting with the FIFA World Cup quarterfinals. France, Spain, England, and Argentina are through, with huge performances from Mbappé, Rodri, Bellingham, and Julián Álvarez. They discuss who looks like the favorite to lift the trophy and preview the semifinal matchups.

They then shift to the NHL offseason, reacting to the Flyers and Devils matching offer sheets for Leo Carlsson and Barret Hayton, Claude Giroux returning to Ottawa, and the unfortunate news that Connor Bedard will miss four months after suffering a shoulder injury in practice. Plus, is Bowen Byram now the face of the Blackhawks?

The boys also dive into the latest Oilers news, including Colton Dach’s new deal, Edmonton’s remaining cap space, free agent targets like Patrick Kane, Vladimir Tarasenko, and Anthony Mantha, potential trade options, and why it’s finally time to move on from Tristan Jarry.
To wrap things up, they preview UFC 329, with Conor McGregor making his long-awaited return and Paddy “The Baddy” Pimblett back in action.

episodes.title: Free Agency Went Off the Rails
paragraphs: The boys are back with another packed offseason episode, starting with the FIFA World Cup as the Round of 32 wraps up and the Round of 16 takes shape. They react to Canada’s run, Norway’s shocking upset, and preview the biggest upcoming matchups, including Spain vs Portugal, USA vs Belgium, and Argentina vs Egypt.

Then it’s time to dive into a busy NHL offseason, breaking down the biggest trades, July 1 signings, and the massive offer sheet sent to Leo Carlsson. Which teams have improved the most? Who overpaid? And who still has work to do before training camp?

Finally, the boys take a closer look at the Edmonton Oilers’ offseason. From new additions and key re-signings to moving on from Darnell Nurse, they discuss whether Edmonton has done enough to become a legitimate Stanley Cup contender while still sitting on nearly $6 million in cap space.

episodes.title: Draft Day (Live)
paragraphs: The boys are back with one of the biggest offseason episodes yet, breaking down all the blockbuster moves from around the NHL. They react to the trades involving Simon Nemec, Jordan Kyrou, Bowen Byram, Alex Tuch, Valeri Nichushkin, Olen Zellweger, Pavel Dorofeyev, JJ Peterka, Mason McTavish, and Sebastian Cossa, discussing which teams got better, which overpaid, and which moves could shape the league for years to come.

They also shift to the NBA to react to two massive deals, with LaMelo Ball heading to Minnesota and Giannis Antetokounmpo joining the Miami Heat in a trade that could completely reshape the Eastern Conference.

To wrap up the season, the boys reveal their Player of the Season voting. After months of weekly Player of the Week selections, the final standings are in, with Connor McDavid taking the crown, followed by Nikita Kucherov and Mitch Marner.

episodes.title: FIFA is Here
paragraphs: The boys are back with their official NHL Awards Predictions, debating every major trophy from the Hart and Art Ross to the Norris, Vezina, Calder, and Conn Smythe. Is McDavid still the best player in the world? Does Kucherov deserve the Hart? Is Matthew Schaefer already a lock for the Calder? The takes are flying.

They also preview Canada’s massive World Cup clash against Switzerland, discuss Egypt vs New Zealand, and break down the latest trade involving Chuckles, along with their predictions for the top three picks in the upcoming NHL Draft.

On the Oilers front, Edmonton locks up Jason Dickinson and Connor Murphy to long-term deals, Mike Babcock appears set to be introduced as head coach, and the guys discuss whether a Darnell Nurse trade happens before or after the draft, with Pittsburgh, Boston, and Los Angeles emerging as possible destinations.
The episode wraps up with Leafs news, Hockey Hall of Fame reactions, and Player of the Week honors going to Jordan Staal after a dominant six-game stretch.

episodes.title: Hurricane Staal Wins (Watch Along Repost)
paragraphs: The boys are back with another Watch Along episode, this time following Carolina vs Vegas live while breaking down one of the biggest stories of the offseason: Darnell Nurse has reportedly requested a trade. They discuss potential landing spots, including Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, and Los Angeles, and try to figure out what a realistic return could look like for Edmonton.

They also check in on the World Cup, reacting to Germany’s dominant 7-1 win, Brazil and Morocco playing to a draw, and Canada’s disappointing result against Bosnia & Herzegovina. Plus, they preview Canada’s upcoming matchup against Qatar and discuss what the group standings could look like moving forward.

episodes.title: Sin City Magic
paragraphs: The boys break down what has become an absolute treat of a Stanley Cup Final, with wild games, momentum swings, and superstar performances taking center stage. They debate whether Mitch Marner has already done enough to win the Conn Smythe, regardless of who ends up lifting the Cup, and discuss the impact of veterans like Dylan Larkin on the biggest stage.
They also shift over to the NBA Finals, where the Knicks head into Madison Square Garden with a 2-0 series lead and a chance to put one hand on the trophy.

To wrap things up, the boys make their World Cup of Hockey predictions, taking a closer look at Canada’s group featuring Switzerland, Bosnia & Herzegovina, and Qatar, while discussing who could challenge for gold.

episodes.title: One Step from the Cup
paragraphs: The boys break down the latest playoff action, starting with Colorado vs Vegas, where Mitch Marner and Carter Hart continue to lead the charge while Vegas searches for answers. They also dive into Carolina vs Montreal, discussing Ehlers’ impact, Dobes’ heroics, and why the Canadiens ultimately fell short.
Beyond the NHL playoffs, they check in on the World Championship, react to the NBA Finals, and preview what could be an incredible Stanley Cup Final matchup.

The episode also touches on the Rockets winning the Memorial Cup before wrapping up with Player of the Week honors. Carter Hart takes home the award after going 4-0 with a .944 save percentage, while Logan Stankoven earns honourable mention after another strong playoff performance.

episodes.title: Pressure is a Privilege
paragraphs: The boys break down Game 7 between Montreal and Buffalo, highlighting the biggest difference makers and the players who disappeared under pressure. From Alexander Newhook stepping up for the Habs to Dahlin doing everything he could for Buffalo, they go through the impact players from both sides.

They also give an update on the Bruce Cassidy coaching situation, shift into the World Championship conversation with Canada, Switzerland, and the USA, and discuss why Macklin Celebrini keeping the “C” matters so much. Plus, Bouchard and Nurse have been cooking for Team Canada in Switzerland.
The episode wraps with previews of the upcoming playoff series and reactions to everything that’s happened around the league so far.

episodes.title: Knoblauch Fired?!?
paragraphs: The boys break down another wild night of playoff hockey, going series by series to hand out the most and least impactful players. From Mitch Marner taking over against Vegas to MacKinnon dominating Minnesota and Jackson Blake continuing to shine for Carolina, there’s no shortage of stars stepping up — and others disappearing.

They also dive into league news, including possible landing spots for Bruce Cassidy, the growing case for Matthew Schaefer as the unanimous Calder winner, the shocking firing of Knoblauch, and Vegas forfeiting a second-round pick.

The episode wraps with a preview of Sabres vs Canadiens Game 7, a playoff edition of Guess the Player, and Player of the Week honors going to Pavel Dorofeyev, with Alexander Newhook earning HM after a huge week.

episodes.title: The Leafs Future Looks… Interesting with Eric Sabouri and Zach Jones
paragraphs: The boys are joined by Zach Jones and Eric Sabouri to break down a packed week of hockey talk. They dive into the future of the Maple Leafs, what direction the franchise should take around Matthews, Chyka, and their draft capital, plus what teams should do if they land the chance to draft Gavin McKenna.
Then it’s full awards season debate mode with Hart, Ted Lindsay, Vezina, Norris, Selke, and Calder discussions — including who deserves the trophies and which players got completely snubbed.

They also get an outsider perspective on the Oilers, recap the latest playoff action including Colorado going up 2-0, Carolina’s sweep, Vegas dominating, and Montreal battling back, before previewing the next slate of games.

episodes.title: Playoff Fraud Check
paragraphs: The boys break down another wild stretch of Stanley Cup Playoff action, going series by series and calling out the most and least impactful players. From Jackson Lacombe and Anaheim’s fourth line stepping up against the Oilers, to Brett Howden leading Vegas, and Jakub Dobes standing on his head for Tampa, it’s a full playoff stock report.

They dive into every matchup including Dallas vs Minnesota, Flyers vs Penguins, and Tampa vs Montreal, highlighting who’s carrying their teams and who’s disappearing under pressure. Plus, some insane playoff games across Avs–Minnesota, Ducks–Vegas, and the Carolina series.
The conversation shifts to what’s next for the Oilers, with bold ideas on roster changes, potential targets like McCann, Malkin, and Tuch, and tough questions around injuries and depth.

episodes.title: Oilers on the Brink
paragraphs: The boys break down the first round of the Stanley Cup Playoffs, handing out awards for the most and least impactful players in each series so far. They dive into Carolina vs Ottawa, highlighting Taylor Hall’s huge impact, Ullmark keeping the Sens alive, and who hasn’t shown up when it matters most.

They also review Avalanche vs Kings, where Scott Wedgewood has stolen the spotlight, while key names on both sides continue to struggle. Plus, a full playoff scoreboard update with Tampa vs Montreal tied, Buffalo and Philly taking control, Dallas vs Minnesota deadlocked, Utah leading, and the Oilers situation still up in the air.
Finally, they preview the next slate of games and wrap things up with Player of the Week honors: Taylor Hall, with Matt Duchene earning honourable mention after a big week of his own.

episodes.title: And Then There Were 16
paragraphs: The boys put their takes on trial in a full Predictions Review episode, looking back at preseason standings, division forecasts, and the teams that surprised everyone across the Atlantic, Metro, Central, and Pacific. Who got it right, who missed badly, and which fanbases ended up living their worst fears?

Then it shifts to the Stanley Cup Playoffs with first-round predictions and the biggest storylines heading into the postseason. Draisaitl and Dickinson are back, the Battle of Pennsylvania is here, and the headline nobody expected: Carter Hart gets the start tonight against Utah.
They wrap things up with Player of the Week honors, giving it to Porter Martone after his Game 1 winner, while Frederik Andersen earns honourable mention after a 22-save shutout.
Receipts are in, playoff chaos is here, and the takes are flying on Brothers in the Box.

episodes.title: Clinchmas
paragraphs: The boys recap March Madness as Michigan takes it all and UConn falls short, then shift to a huge moment for Edmonton as the Oilers have a chance to clinch. They break down Evan Bouchard’s push for 100 points — something only elite defensemen like Leetch and Karlsson have done — and react to McDavid’s 5-point night putting him right back in the Hart conversation.

They also preview the NBA Play-In and Playoffs, check in on The Masters with Rory leading and Scheffler lurking, and run through quick hits around the league — including Caufield hitting 50 and TJ Hughes signing with Colorado.

episodes.title: Bouchard for the Norris
paragraphs: March Madness heats up as the boys react to UCLA winning it all and preview the final matchup between Michigan and UConn. Who takes it?

Back in the NHL, the Pacific Division race is tighter than ever with the Oilers, Ducks, and Knights separated by just a single point. After a tough loss to Vegas, the guys break down what Edmonton needs to clinch and whether they’re in trouble.

They also dive into the Norris Trophy debate, reacting to Kevin Bieksa’s comments on Evan Bouchard and making the case for who really deserves it, plus a major coaching change with Roy out and DeBoer in.
The episode wraps with playoff clinchers, surprising eliminations (yes… Florida), and Player of the Week: Jack Hughes, with Rickard Rakell earning HM after a huge scoring run.

episodes.title: Lay it on the Line
paragraphs: The boys break down a massive week for the Oilers, with a strong win over Anaheim and an even bigger statement win against Vegas. With just 8 games left, the Pacific Division race is heating up — and the current lines are finally clicking. They also debate where Draisaitl fits back in once he returns.

Around the league, they react to Bruce Cassidy being fired and John Tortorella stepping in, plus dive into the Aquilini controversy involving alleged labour violations tied to vineyard operations in Washington state.
They wrap up with March Madness Final Four predictions, a quick Raising Cane’s review, and Player of the Week honors: Jake Guentzel, with Pavel Zacha earning HM.

episodes.title: Gary Broke the NHL
paragraphs: The boys react to the World Cup of Hockey officially being announced, with Edmonton, Calgary, and Prague named as host cities. They then dive into the huge Oilers news: Leon Draisaitl is out for the season for now after a lower-body injury in Nashville, with hopes he could still return for the playoffs. The guys break down what the injury might be, what it means for Edmonton, and whether Leon should even play if he’s not fully healthy.

They also cover AJ Greer’s suspension, react to the chaos of March Madness, including near-upsets, busted brackets, and the last few perfect brackets standing, and debate whether the NHL playoff format needs a serious change.

episodes.title: Gudas the Goon
paragraphs: The boys break down another Oilers update, including the controversial Nathan MacKinnon hit on Ingram, why two good periods of defence still aren’t enough, and the growing list of injuries affecting the lineup — Janmark, Colton Dach, RNH, and Emberson. They also react to the Radko Gudas hit, his 5-game suspension, and the shocking news of Auston Matthews being out for the season.

The conversation shifts to the World Baseball Classic quarterfinals, where the guys build their brackets and debate whether the Dominican Republic could get upset. They also cover major NFL trade news, including the Maxx Crosby deal and Geno Smith returning to the New York Jets.
To wrap things up, they give their Player of the Week to Alexis Lafrenière after a hat trick and seven points in four games, with Nikita Kucherov earning honourable mention.

episodes.title: The Oilers Forgot a Goalie Again
paragraphs: It’s Trade Deadline Recap time, and the boys break down the biggest moves around the NHL. From Edmonton acquiring Connor Murphy and Jason Dickinson to Utah landing MacKenzie Weegar, Dallas grabbing Tyler Myers and Michael Bunting, and Buffalo loading up on defence with Logan Stanley and Luke Schenn, the deadline had no shortage of chaos.
They also talk about the Oilers’ situation, why the goaltending issue still hasn’t been fixed, and why a first-round exit is becoming a real possibility unless something changes in the offseason.

Beyond the NHL, the guys preview the World Baseball Classic, discuss the format and their favorites to win, and react to massive NFL trades including DJ Moore being moved and Maxx Crosby heading to Baltimore.

episodes.title: Step Up or Get Out
paragraphs: The boys dive into a full Oilers update, breaking down who needs to step up — including Jarry and Frederic — and who’s been answering the call, with strong play from Matt Savoie, Ingram, and Podz.

They review the LA Kings, discuss Paul Coffey stepping in as assistant coach on defence, and get into trade rumours around the league. From Vinny to Minnesota, OEL or Faulk potentially heading to Edmonton, a massive OEL + McMann retained package, Kulak trade chatter, and more — it’s rumor season in full swing.
They wrap with Guess the Player and Player of the Week honors: Matt Boldy after a big two-game stretch, with Brayden Point earning HM.
Trade chaos, Oilers pressure, and league movement — classic Brothers in the Box.

episodes.title: One Game for Gold
paragraphs: The boys recap the Olympics heading into the final day — breaking down the quarterfinals and semifinals, Finland taking bronze, Slovakia’s unreal run, and Canada’s women falling short. They update Canada’s medal count (5G, 6S, 9B) and preview the Gold Medal matchup, highlighting key storylines around Morrissey, Thompson, and Crosby.

They also cover NHL news during the Olympic break, including trades, Lekkermäki’s season-ending injury, Rantanen’s lower-body concern, and Matt Savoie’s brief Condors appearance. Plus, WHL Prospect Game reactions and Gavin McKenna’s ridiculous 8-point night.

episodes.title: Is Anyone Beating Canada?
paragraphs: The boys break down the latest from the Olympics, including a massive Canada vs. USA showdown and why Canada might be looking unstoppable right now. With hockey at an elite level across the tournament, they debate why the USA hasn’t impressed in what looked like an easy group.

They also update the medal standings, highlight Italy’s strong showing as host nation, and react to key injuries — including Josh Morrissey and Kevin Fiala, who is now out for the season after surgery.
The episode wraps with Player of the Week, as two stars are currently on pace to challenge the Olympic points record, with Juraj Slafkovsky and Connor McDavid earning honourable mention.

episodes.title: Tampa Runs the League (Again)
paragraphs: The boys break down the wild Gavin McKenna situation, from felony charges being laid on February 4th to everything being dropped two days later — including the full context behind what actually happened. From there, it’s trade season chaos with Panarin heading to LA, incentive-heavy conditions, and the Lightning starting to look like a legit contender again.

They react to a completely unhinged NBA trade deadline, debate Team Canada replacement decisions, and unpack a blunt Leon Draisaitl rant calling out Edmonton’s defensive issues. The episode wraps with hot takes, Olympic chaos, and Player of the Week honors: Nikita Kucherov, with Jack Eichel earning HM.

episodes.title: Game of the Year (Stadium Series)
paragraphs: The boys run another watch-along episode as the NHL goes absolutely nuclear in January — 31 hat tricks in 31 days from Jan 22 to Jan 30. The league is buzzing.

They break down the Oilers winning three straight, including a wild comeback against the Sharks, and debate whether Edmonton actually looked good doing it. Trade talk follows with Bobby McMann’s value, a look back at the history of the Stadium Series, and a debate you didn’t know you needed: Is Dylan Larkin a top-10 captain in the NHL?
The episode wraps with Player of the Week: Evan Bouchard after a historic night vs Washington (4G, 7A over 4 games), with Travis Konecny earning HM after a clutch hat trick to keep the streak alive.

episodes.title: Sharks Winning the Cup?!?
paragraphs: The boys jump straight into Responding to Hot Takes, reacting to some wild ones — including the Sharks winning the Cup, playoff concerns around Ingram and Jarry’s save percentages, and rumours of Evander Kane being moved to Colorado or Dallas.

Trade talk heats up with a deep dive into Rasmus Andersson to Vegas, breaking down a potential return featuring Zack Whitecloud, top defence prospect Abram Wiebe, and conditional picks that escalate if the Knights win the Cup. They also discuss Kiefer Sherwood to San Jose for multiple second-rounders and young defenseman Cole Clayton.
The episode wraps with Guess the Player and Player of the Week honors: Kirill Kaprizov after a massive week capped by an OT winner, with Ryan O’Reilly earning honourable mention.

episodes.title: 90 Day Check-in
paragraphs: The boys open with an update on Leon Draisaitl, who’s away attending to family in Germany and expected back next week. From there, it’s a fan-based segment and a deep dive into sleeper fantasy picks you should be targeting right now — from underrated defensemen like Zadorov and Lauzon, to forward value plays like Dawson Mercer, Podz, and Collin Graf, plus sneaky goalie options including Connor Ingram and Trent Miner.
They also introduce Guess That Player, before wrapping up with Player of the Week honors: Jack Eichel after a dominant week, with Tage Thompson earning HM after stuffing the scoresheet.

episodes.title: Dougie? Gone
paragraphs: Trade buzz takes over as the boys break down the Dougie Hamilton situation, exploring what a deal could look like for Carolina, Buffalo, San Jose, or even Toronto. From there, it’s a full Oilers update as Edmonton’s special teams dominate — a league-best 33.9% power play and a steady penalty kill — while Connor McDavid extends his point streak to 18 games and Leon Draisaitl hits the 1,000-point milestone.

They also highlight Trent Miner’s first NHL win and shutout, react to Philip Broberg’s 6x8M extension, and pivot to a quick look at the NFL playoffs. The episode wraps with Player of the Week honors: David Pastrňák after a massive week, with Connor McDavid earning honourable mention.

episodes.title: International Hockey Week
paragraphs: The boys continue their Olympic coverage with a breakdown of the remaining rosters from USA, Finland, and Sweden, reacting to strengths, surprises, and medal potential. They also preview the World Juniors semifinals, highlighting key matchups and players to watch.

The episode rounds out with an Oilers update, a review of the Winter Classic, and Player of the Week honors: Nikita Kucherov after a ridiculous 12-point week, with Auston Matthews earning HM following a hat trick performance.

episodes.title: New Year's Eve Special - Olympic Rosters
paragraphs: The boys ring in New Year’s Eve with a full breakdown of the Olympic hockey rosters, reacting to Team Canada, USA, Finland, Sweden, Czechia, and Germany. They debate roster strengths, surprise omissions, medal favorites, and which nations are being slept on heading into the tournament.

episodes.title: From Injuries to Knockouts
paragraphs: The injury bug continues to sweep the league as the boys break down key updates on Connor Bedard, Tristan Jarry, Frank Nazar, and Seth Jarvis. Trade talk follows with reactions to Danault heading to Montreal, Marchment moving to Columbus, and growing speculation around an Oilers goaltending move.

They also react to Jake Paul vs. Anthony Joshua, debating the knockout and whether the fight felt legitimate. The episode closes with a fun Christmas draft segment and Player of the Week, as Connor McDavid repeats after another dominant stretch, with Matt Boldy earning honourable mention.

episodes.title: Have no Fear, Jarry is Here
paragraphs: Trade chaos is here. The boys break down blockbuster NHL trade ideas involving Jarry, Quinn Hughes, and Spencer Stastny, before diving into an Oilers update as Jarry shines in his first game and Edmonton starts to look dangerous again. Is this finally the spark?

episodes.title: NHL Wrapped
paragraphs: The Oilers’ December heater is alive as the boys break down Edmonton’s turnaround, injury updates, and Eshan officially winning the Bouchard bet. Then it’s time for NHL Wrapped: the biggest moments of 2025, top plays of the year, the wildest player moves, and fanbase mood rankings — from the happiest to the most chaotic to pure depression season.
Finally, the guys crown their Player of the Week: Mikko Rantanen, with MacKinnon earning HM.A full year of hockey chaos packed into one episode of Brothers in the Box.

episodes.title: Do the Oilers Survive This? (Watch-Along vs. Kraken)
paragraphs: Live reactions to Oilers–Kraken, Edmonton’s goalie crisis, trade options, injuries, and Keller’s emotional game — plus Hagel’s huge week and Cooley’s explosion.

episodes.title: Do the leafs really need Matthews?
paragraphs: PWHL Opening Night OT thriller, Leafs without Matthews, the Rantanen–Romanov hit, Olympic roster chaos, and Alex Ovechkin’s monster week. Guentzel gets HM.

episodes.title: Tims Packs Pulled, Espresso Spilled, Oilers Thrilled
paragraphs: Nespresso espresso, Tim's packs, Oilers wins, and stars on a heater. The boys rip packs, break down Hyman’s big return, Roslovic and McDavid’s hot streaks, and name Jason Robertson their Player of the Week (with Davo as HM).

episodes.title: Celebrate Celebrini (and worry about McDrai)
paragraphs: Celebrini vs. Bedard, Oilers workload worries, Skinner’s future, Ducks kids cooking, Team Canada jersey talk — plus our first Player of the Week: Wyatt Johnston (with Cutter Gauthier as HM). Classic Brothers in the Box vibes.

episodes.title: Jack Micheals Jinxed Us
paragraphs: Blue Jays pain. Oilers winning. Celebrini cooking. The guys rant about the Jays collapse, break down the Oilers’ November heater, and revisit the Rantanen trade saga.

episodes.title: Frustration on the Ice, Fire in the Booth
paragraphs: Eshan and Ilyas break down the Oilers’ slump, McDavid’s frustration, and Caulfield’s ref comments — plus World Series talk and Blue Jays updates.

episodes.title: Live Reactions: Oilers vs Devils Watch-Along
paragraphs: Eshan and Ilyas go live during the Oilers–Devils game for a special watch-along episode, reacting to goals, breakdowns, and hot takes on Bouchard, Schaefer, McKenna, and more. Real-time emotion, sharp analysis, and classic Brothers in the Box banter.

episodes.title: Opening Night
paragraphs: In Episode 5, the brothers mix Thanksgiving talk with opening night reactions — from Bedard’s debut to Florida’s start — plus series predictions, Oilers storylines, and early-season takes on the rest of the league.

episodes.title: Mascot Madness
paragraphs: In Episode 4, Eshan and Ilyas cover AJ Greer’s Fine, Knoblauch’s new deal with the Oilers, and settle the ultimate debate: which NHL mascot would win in a fight?

episodes.title: Prediction or Pipe Dream?
paragraphs: In Episode 3, Eshan and Ilyas break down Podkolzin’s and McTavish’s new contracts, Barkov’s season-altering injury, and Florida’s playoff hopes. They also give bold division previews and make their picks for every NHL award heading into 2025-26.

episodes.title: Captain Mayhem
paragraphs: Eshan and Ilyas dive into J.T. Miller’s new captaincy with the Rangers, Mason McTavish trade buzz, and Connor McDavid’s uncertain future in Edmonton. They break down Stuart Skinner’s offseason transformation, Kopitar’s retirement, and tough league news, before closing with Quinn Hughes’ contract questions in Vancouver. A mix of hot takes, tributes, and banter you won’t want to miss.

episodes.title: Pilot
paragraphs: In the debut episode of Brothers in the Box, the guys dive straight into hockey’s hottest storylines. They kick things off with a full recap of the Oilers rookie game, breaking down standout performances and debating which prospects are ready to make the leap. The conversation expands to Edmonton’s overall team strategy and potential lineup changes heading into the season.

Around the league, they discuss Marc-André Fleury’s emotional return to Pittsburgh, goaltending situations that could shape contenders, and the uncertainty surrounding Carter Hart’s future. The episode also unpacks Spencer Knight’s new contract, what it means for Chicago, and whether Corey Perry still has a place in the NHL as his career winds down.
Packed with insights, bold takes, and some classic back-and-forth banter, this episode sets the tone for a season full of hockey talk from the Brothers in the Box.
